name: Heliopolitan Atum / Ennead creation tradition
source_label: Heliopolitan creation tradition in Pyramid Texts and later Egyptian sources

earliest_archaeological_evidence.note: The Pyramid Texts appear in royal pyramid chambers from the late Fifth Dynasty onward; Cambridge sources place the corpus broadly in late Dynasty V–VI.

earliest_written_attestation.note: Old Kingdom Pyramid Texts are the earliest written witnesses used here for Atum/Heliopolitan cosmogonic material.

surviving_manuscript_date.note: The earliest witnesses are monumental pyramid inscriptions rather than manuscripts; this slot records the surviving physical textual evidence.

tradition_internal_claim.note: The tradition concerns primordial creation and divine genealogy rather than a calendar-dated event.

estimated_oral_origin.method: No absolute oral-origin date is assigned. The first surviving written witnesses do not establish when the tradition first circulated.

dating.dating_summary: Heliopolitan creation is already attested in Old Kingdom Pyramid Texts. Those inscriptions securely anchor the surviving evidence while the tradition's prior oral or compositional history remains unknown.

notes: Ancient Egyptian creation theology was plural. This record complements, rather than replaces, the separate Memphite/Ptah record.
